items.stem: Why must a variable mapped to a hardware status register be declared volatile in C?

options.text: Because the hardware can change it independently, so the compiler must not cache or optimise away reads
options.rationale: Correct: volatile forces each access, since hardware may change the register at any time.

options.text: Because it makes the access faster
options.rationale: Volatile prevents optimisation; it does not speed access up.

options.text: Because volatile encrypts the register value
options.rationale: Volatile has nothing to do with encryption.

options.text: Because the OS requires all variables to be volatile
options.rationale: Only hardware- or concurrency-affected values need volatile.

items.explanation: Correct: volatile forces each access, since hardware may change the register at any time.

items.stem: Which TWO practices keep an interrupt handler safe and responsive? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Keep the handler short and defer heavy work to a bottom half
options.rationale: Correct: short handlers plus deferred work keep latency low.

options.text: Avoid blocking or sleeping inside the handler
options.rationale: Correct: handlers must not sleep, as they run in interrupt context.

options.text: Perform long file I/O directly in the handler
options.rationale: Long I/O in a handler blocks other interrupts.

options.text: Acquire a sleeping lock inside the handler
options.rationale: Sleeping locks are unsafe in interrupt context.

items.explanation: Correct: short handlers plus deferred work keep latency low.

items.stem: During boot, what is the typical responsibility of firmware before the operating system takes over?

options.text: Initialise core hardware and load the OS or bootloader
options.rationale: Correct: firmware brings up essential hardware and hands off to the OS/bootloader.
User applications run later, under the OS.
The UI is an OS/application concern, not firmware's boot role.

options.text: Manage virtual memory paging for processes
options.rationale: Paging is an OS responsibility, established after boot.

items.explanation: Correct: firmware brings up essential hardware and hands off to the OS/bootloader.
